tagline: Forty-two miles of red buttes between Medicine Lodge and Coldwater.
intro: Out of Medicine Lodge, US 160 runs west 42 miles to Coldwater across ground that does not look like the rest of the Kansas plains: red buttes and mesas, small steep canyons, and sinkholes. The straight road is the newer one. Until the early 1940s, US 160 went the long way around by Wilmore, Sun City and Lake City.

The red is iron, oxidized in beds laid down in a dry Permian basin where shallow playas flooded, dried out and left their gypsum behind. Where the gypsum has dissolved underneath, the ground has fallen in.

moments.title: Medicine Lodge
moments.text: Near here in October 1867 the United States signed treaties with five southern Plains tribes, and since 1961 the town has restaged the peace council in a pageant every three years.

moments.title: Carrie Nation House
moments.text: Carrie Nation was living in this house, now open to visitors, in 1900 when she set out for the saloons of Kiowa with rocks she called smashers.

moments.title: Coldwater
moments.text: Laid out in 1884 by six men from Harper County and named for Coldwater, Michigan, it was made the Comanche County seat the next winter.
